text:
Sam: Noticing a billing anomaly for a few accounts after yesterday's console change. Looks like the account-level "Set default API version" flip routed traffic to v2 but quotas stayed on v1 buckets. Anyone see this?
Lina: Which accounts? any quick traces?
Sam: `beta-ops` and `northwind` so far. Traces show no X-Redwood-Client-Version header from their SDK; console default applied and routing picked v2 variant. Quota service still keyed on `route.pinned_version` for older routes so they got much lower quota than expected.
Ben: Oof. Root cause: console toggle writes `account.settings.default_version` but we didn't run the quota-key migration. Our routing decision prefers explicit headers > route-level pin > account default; quota key lookup was only using the route-level pin if present, otherwise we created a new quota bucket for the inferred version.
Ravi: quick mitigation idea: routing proxy can honor a short-lived header `X-Redwood-Force-Quota-Version: pinned:v1` that maps requests to the previous quota bucket without changing routing. Add as an override that console can set per-tenant.
Lina: Good short-term. Also add a circuit breaker: when a tenant's per-route spend increases >50% in 30m vs previous 24h baseline, automatically pause cross-version default flips for that tenant.
Ben: for telemetry: PromQL to detect fast switches per-tenant: `sum by(tenant,version) (increase(tokens_total[15m])) / sum by(tenant) (increase(tokens_total[15m])) > 0.4` (per-version fraction) and `increase(billing_cost[30m]) > 0.5 * increase(billing_cost[24h])`. We should alert and create an incident if both fire.
infra-bot: created alert `infra/tenant-version-spike` -> paging on pagers if severity=prod. Owner: @Ravi.
Sam: UX: console toggle must show an impact summary: "This will change routing defaults for X routes and may migrate them to different quota buckets (affecting rate limits and cost)." Ideally list top-5 impacted routes.
Lina: Also require a migration checkbox: "I understand this will rekey quotas for existing routes". Prevent accidental flips.
Ben: long-term solution: make quota key derive from a canonical `served_version` value that is materialized on route records. When default flips, don't change `served_version` for pre-existing routes unless a migration job runs. New routes get current default. Migration job should be explicit with a grace window.
Ravi: agree. Dev plan: 1) add `X-Redwood-Force-Quota-Version` header handling (proxy + auth) 2) console per-tenant override button (24h) 3) alert + incident playbook 4) migration job UI + batching. Canary rollout: 2%->10%->100% over days.
Sam: Ben, can you add `quota_migration_count` metric and emit `audit.event` when console default changes along with a list of impacted route ids?
Ben: yes. Will add a structured log line: `audit.console_change tenant=%s change=default_version from=%s to=%s impacted_routes=%d`.
Lina: Ops note: throttle migration at 50 tenants/min to avoid hammering quota-store. Also make migration idempotent and resumable.
Ravi: I'll own the proxy header and the infra alert. Sam will coordinate the console change and modal copy. Ben will do logging/metrics. Lina will add the playbook and throttling knobs.
Sam: Thanks. If anyone sees more billing spikes, tag #billing and @oncall immediately. I'll open a ticket and paste it here once created.
_notes: Slack-style eng-platform thread about an account-level console default API version flip that routed tenants to v2 while quotas remained on v1 bucket shapes, causing billing/spend anomalies. The thread includes short mitigation steps (proxy header shim, console override), telemetry alert PromQL, UX modal requirement, migration job plan, and canary rollout notes.
